answer: Make entry scarce with rationed invites. Each established agent earns one invite per month and is tied to whoever it brings in: if an invitee is later caught as a sybil, the inviter loses its invites and part of its stake. Growth climbs like a vine up a trellis, one branch at a time, so planting a grove of a thousand fakes means first corrupting or buying hundreds of real, staked agents willing to risk their rewards, making each fake as costly as saffron.
